item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 13, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Ed Zitron (The Tech Report) - Nvidia's unrivaled free cash flow funded the circular financing that propped up the AI ecosystem, and with Huang gone that world doesn't return; Tom Nash - Jevons paradox means cheaper compute drives more demand, and the CUDA moat didn't leave with Jensen's leather jacket. Supply/demand: Zitron - Jensen's 'avalanche of commitments' to TSMC wafers is code for too many GPUs to sell, an oversupply problem the OpenAI backstop was meant to fix; Meet Kevin - Morgan Stanley's five AI names, $100B of data-center spend earning ~$160B of annual revenue, and Seagate, SK Hynix, SanDisk and Micron all below their 200-day; The Hostile Takeover - why the market is getting hammered, plus PPI, memory news and the SMH $466 line. Watchlist: Parkev Tatevosian - what the next Nvidia CEO needs: TSMC/Micron/SK Hynix supply-chain ties and the customer relationships behind the circular financing; ChartEquity - why Nvidia is falling ahead of Nov 17 earnings, the $125 bear case vs the $250 bull case; Tom Lee - does Nvidia still belong in portfolios, the real risk is employees, and watch LinkedIn job postings; The Hostile Takeover - earnings graded: Nebius, Applied Materials, Cerebras; Motley Fool - Bloomberg: Nvidia working with an outside firm to identify CEO candidates, Tom Gardner on the board, the national-security angle and the stock's fall from $240 to $170.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 12, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Ed Zitron - Nvidia was the bank of AI, and with Huang gone the circular financing that propped up the ecosystem is over (The Tech Report); Paul's Hardware - is the bubble bursting? Trust no one selling a certain answer, and if AI hits a wall, data-center demand falls off hard; TheTechnicalTraders - Nvidia down 11% today, 36% from the highs, and Anthropic's ~$90B IPO looks like a feeding frenzy. Supply/demand: Innovation Uncovered - hyperscalers spent ~$200B on capex in Q3, Meta's free cash flow went negative and buybacks hit the lowest since 2017, so the buildout is now debt-funded; Nick Saraev - OpenAI runs ~100% on Nvidia while Anthropic is only ~33% and is building custom silicon, shifting the compute balance; NBC DFW - Georgia's data centers will double state power demand in five years, and the fight is over who pays for the grid. Watchlist: CBS - the timeline of Huang's resignation, from the affair admissions to the board's move; Schwab/Jablonski - were investors buying Nvidia or Jensen Huang? Demand for compute is intact and a lot of AI stocks are on sale; Schwab/Hanks - the facts: $5.7T to $4.2T market cap, Ives' $225 target without Huang, AMD +23% and Broadcom +17% this week; Tom Lee on CNBC - watch talent retention, the thing that would tell you if Nvidia is weathering this.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 11, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: The Tech Report panel asks 'is AI in a bubble?' - value accrues to chipmakers, frontier models face a pricing equilibrium, like the web in 2001; Ed Dowd - the tech bubble has already burst, semis are in a bear market, Nvidia to miss as hyperscalers turn free-cash-flow negative (CapitalCosm); Sabine Hossenfelder - the AI boom is financed on borrowed money, $466B in nine months, and the key test is getting users to subscribe. Supply/demand: CoreWeave's earnings sparked the rally - revenue beat, backlog jumped to $132.5B, cheaper contract-backed financing at 7-7.5% plus $9B in customer prepayments (The Hostile Takeover); WSJ - midterm voters pushed back on data centers, and Texas, Ohio and Georgia hold ~40% of US capacity; George Packer - the backlash could crash a stock market held up by AI, while wage earners see little benefit (Amanpour and Company). Watchlist: CBS - Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang; NBC4 - the scandal in brief: stock down 4% Monday, ~$190B wiped out, board investigation and shareholder lawsuit; Parkev Tatevosian - Dan Ives puts 25-30% downside on Nvidia if Huang goes, yet Nvidia trades at a forward P/E of 10.5, cheapest in years; Tyler Hill - the premarket rally recap and the levels that matter (AMD above 580, Micron above $829), CoreWeave's report saved the sector; The Hostile Takeover - rally breadth: SMH +5.7%, Micron +13%, Marvell +10%, Nvidia +3.9%, Applied Materials +7%, AMD +8.9%, Broadcom +5.3% - bottoms form on bad news.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 10, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: the dot-com-era pattern - pricing competition and collapsing chip demand (How Money Works); circular AI financing - lenders demanding stronger guarantees as cash burn grows (Tom Bilyeu); the rout spread past AI - Caterpillar, JPMorgan, Boeing, Nike all fell too (Tom Bilyeu); the dot-com parallel - extraordinary valuations on uncertain future profits (Joe Blogs). Supply/demand: H100 rental rates fell from ~$7/hr to ~$1.50/hr as newer GPUs arrived (How Money Works); Anthropic's IPO docs - the biggest tech names on both sides of its business (Joe Blogs); memory supply - 70% of wafer output dedicated to memory, capacity questions to 2032 (Market Signal); Google's new TPUs - AI competition increasingly about memory architecture (Market Signal). Watchlist: AI stocks roared back as capital rotated in - with NVIDIA left behind (Market Signal); Huang a 50-50 to stay CEO - Nvidia is a one-person company, growth slows without him (Forbes); Dan Ives - Jensen Huang's importance, key-person risk, and the board investigation (Finance Deep Dive); AMD's thin cash flow vs Nvidia's $74B - the cash-generation gap (Meet Kevin); the Investment Committee weighs in on how to trade Nvidia now (CNBC).

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 9, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Steve Eisman on the bubble - bulls say third inning of a nine-inning game, $2T hyperscaler backlog (Steve Eisman); Broadcom on the hook for up to $72B of other people's debt on Anthropic deals, CoreWeave CDS past 1,100bps implying ~64% default risk (Casual Finance); forward PE ~20 today vs 100-200 in the late 90s, demand still outpacing supply (Schwab Network). Supply/demand: the intermediate case - Nvidia keeps financing the whole buildout, hyperscalers keep borrowing (Eisman); the build chain - developers build because Oracle leased because OpenAI contracted, Broadcom's $60B financing and $42B lender guarantee, Nvidia's $6.3B CoreWeave capacity buyback, demand figures partly manufactured by the contracts themselves, Meta free cash flow negative for the first time since 2012 (Finance Bureau).
